messages:
incident-bot: P1 ALERT: runtime-prod: sustained worker queue backlog for model-x across us-east-1; user-facing 504s and timeouts increasing. Metrics: queue_depth_p95 > 420, worker_inflight_avg ~ 86, proxy_5xx_rate 2.8% over 5m. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/prod/runtime/model-x

incident-bot: auto-pager triggered. Notifying on-call.

nate: on it. I'm the active on-call. Quick ask: any deploys in last 30m?

sam: none in prod for model-x in last hour. I see a spike in long-context streaming sessions and a handful of orgs doing heavy concurrent streams.

priya: joining. Hypothesis: persistent streaming sessions with very large contexts are filling KV cache and keeping entries pinned; that increases per-request time and causes queue thrash. Live mitigations we should consider: temporary streaming ingress throttles, emergency per-org throttles for top offenders, reduce model-x max_in_flight, and enable early-shed (drop oldest queued) to avoid head-of-line blocking.

tori: +1. Also suggest toggling the keepalive/persistent-connections FF and disabling server-side chunked streaming (it keeps connections alive and KV entries resident). If we blunt the persistent sessions, we free KV memory fast.

nate: plan: 1) apply soft global rate limit on /v1/stream to 300rps, 2) apply emergency per-org token caps for heavy orgs (analytics-labs, big-corp), 3) runtime change: max_in_flight 96->28, queue_timeout 750ms, enable drop-on-full oldest-first, 4) flip persistent-connections=false. We'll do #1 and #4 first since they are fastest. Sam, can you do #4? Priya can you do runtime patch?

sam: doing feature flag flip now. Command:```
redwoodctl flags update --env prod --flag enable-persistent-connections=false --who sam --note "P1 runtime backpressure mitigation"
```

deploy-bot: flags update queued -> rolling to control-plane and proxies (est ~25s).

priya: preparing runtime patch and rollback. Note: lowering max_in_flight will cause some in-flight sessions to be shed; coordinate with CS. Patch command below.

priya:```
# runtime admin API: reduce concurrency and enable drop-on-full
curl -X POST https://runtime-admin.prod.internal/models/model-x/config 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" 
 -d '{"max_in_flight":28,"queue_timeout_ms":750,"drop_policy":"oldest_first"}'
```

nate: Sam — once FF flip finishes, roll out a soft edge-rate limit. Sam or deploy-bot, apply.

sam: applying soft global rate-limit now:```
redwoodctl traffic policy set --scope global --route "/v1/stream" --rate 300rps --burst 60 --mode soft --note "P1 reduce streaming ingress"
```

deploy-bot: traffic policy update in progress -> proxies updated 0/4; target ~40s

priya: runtime API accepted patch, scheduling rolling worker config restart in us-east-1. Watch for shed logs.

sam: traffic policy at 4/4 proxies, in effect. Early delta: aggregate streaming RPS -41% at edge.

nate: good. Priya, status on restarts?

priya: restarts underway. Worker-inflight counts dropping as expected from ~86 to mid-20s on updated nodes. Queue depth down on nodes being patched. However, shed events spiked initially as we enforced drop policy — expected. Overall proxy 504s dipping from 2.8% -> 1.1% in 7m.

cs-bot: Alert: contacting CS champions for analytics-labs and big-corp: summary and mitigations applied. Expected user impact: degraded throughput for sustained streams; short-term throttling & potential dropped requests.

nate: I'm going to create per-org emergency quotas for the two noisy orgs. Priya — if we see any customer escalations, coordinate with CS. Command I'm running:```
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/admin/quotas 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" 
 -d '{"org":"analytics-labs","tokens_per_min":2500,"reason":"P1 runtime ingress mitigation"}'

curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/admin/quotas 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" 
 -d '{"org":"big-corp","tokens_per_min":2000,"reason":"P1 runtime ingress mitigation"}'
```

sam: quotas applied. CS notified.

priya: patched all workers in us-east-1. Observed global queue p95 down from 420 -> 110; worker_inflight_avg down to ~22; 5xxs down to 0.6% in 12m. Things look stable but keep monitoring for rebound.

nate: handoff: I'm going to hand page to Priya for the next 3 hours to watch for reoccurrence while I finish runbook notes. Priya, can you take the pager?

priya: taking pager handoff. Nate — post a quick summary of actions and any outstanding items you want me to watch.

nate: summary for handoff: probable root: long-lived streaming + large contexts pinning KV cache -> per-worker memory pressure and queue thrash. Actions performed: FF disable persistent-connections, global soft rate-limit /v1/stream -> 300rps, per-org emergency quotas for analytics-labs and big-corp, lowered max_in_flight to 28, queue timeout 750ms, enabled drop-on-full oldest-first. Immediate outcome: queue depth & in-flight down, 5xxs remediated to <1%. Outstanding: monitor for cache pressure rebound when we re-enable persistent-connections, schedule follow-up to tune eviction/LRU and investigate client patterns causing large-context streams.

priya: got it. I'll watch dashboards and CS Slack for escalations. If we see spike or customers impacted heavily, we can temporarily raise extra capacity or widen quotas. Also will capture the exact audit log ids.

deploy-bot: ACTION: changes recorded audit_id=aud_20260315_1792354321. Feature flag and traffic policies timestamped.

priya: noted. I'll keep the global rate limit for 30 minutes and reduced max_in_flight for 45 minutes unless things stabilize sooner. If stable for 30m, I'll incrementally relax limits and re-enable persistent-connections behind a safer cache eviction policy.

nate: thanks team. I'll write a short incident stub in ops/incidents and assign a longer postmortem to runtime/infra to dig into cache sizing and client-side streaming behavior.

priya: metrics stable for 14m now. Marking as monitored. :white_check_mark:

cs-bot: CS update: customers notified; two orgs requested status page link and ETA; we've given ~1h window for full restoration and offered workaround (smaller context windows).

priya: will close the page if stable for 45m. Leaving this thread open for audits.
